authority: Aegis owns pipeline, approvals, worktree registration and evidence gates; upstream skills supply craft guidance only.

skills.name: brainstorming
collisions: Preserve the user's approved scope; never treat this skill as a second pipeline or a second approval authority.
Use Aegis discovery/PRD/DEMO gates. Upstream mandatory writing-plans transitions, spec folders and repeated path-approval workflow are not an additional orchestrator.

skills.name: test-driven-development
collisions: Never delete or reset unfamiliar user work to satisfy the upstream delete-untested-code instruction.
Record actual test outcomes with tdd red/green; review why RED failed.

skills.name: systematic-debugging
collisions: Root-cause investigation does not grant production access or permission to change credentials.
Do not copy upstream examples that dump environment values. Log credential presence only, redact private payloads, and target only owned processes.

skills.name: requesting-code-review
collisions: Conductor authorizes reviewers; no recursive persona-spawning or agent-to-agent instructions.
Reviewers receive artifact and contract; their verdict cannot approve a human gate.

skills.name: using-git-worktrees
collisions: Aegis slice registry owns lane caps and worktrees; do not create a second worktree or a second .aegis state.
If isolation is unavailable, stop or record a sequential exception; do not silently build production slices on main.

skills.name: verification-before-completion
collisions: No completion claim without fresh evidence; absent tools mean UNMEASURED, not PASS.
Verification guidance cannot override a failed suite, review blocker or ship gate.
